questions.q:
Retail inflation in India for June 2026 was released on 13 July 2026 by the National Statistics Office on the new CPI series. Consider the following statements:
1. CPI (combined) inflation rose to 4.38% in June 2026, the first time under the new series (base year 2024=100) that it exceeded the RBI's 4% median target.
2. Food inflation measured by the Consumer Food Price Index was 5.32% in June 2026.
3. The RBI's inflation target is 4% with a tolerance band of plus or minus 1 percentage point.
4. The CPI is compiled and released by the Office of the Economic Adviser, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct as per the MoSPI release. The flexible inflation targeting framework sets a 4% target with a band of plus or minus 2 percentage points (2% to 6%), so statement 3 is wrong. CPI comes from MoSPI's National Statistics Office, whereas the Wholesale Price Index is the one compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT.
questions.s: MoSPI CPI press release, 13 Jul 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about industrial output data released in July 2026:
1. The Index of Industrial Production grew 7.3% year-on-year in June 2026, a 23-month high, according to MoSPI's quick estimates.
2. The Index of Industrial Production is compiled and released by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT.
3. On 20 July 2026 the first Index of Core Industries on a new series with base year 2022-23 was released, replacing the 2011-12 series.
4. The new Index of Core Industries covers nine core industries, with iron ore added.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The IIP is a monthly index compiled by the National Statistics Office under MoSPI, so statement 2 is wrong. The Office of the Economic Adviser (DPIIT) compiles the Index of Core Industries, which has been rebased to 2022-23 and now includes iron ore, taking it to nine industries. Rebasing keeps the index aligned with the present structure of the economy.
questions.s: MoSPI IIP release and DPIIT OEA, 20-28 Jul 2026

questions.q:
Match List-I (Union Cabinet decision, July 2026) with List-II (feature):
List-I
A. Semicon 2.0 (India Semiconductor Mission 2.0)
B. Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme
C. National Investment Policy for Urea (NIPU 2026)
D. Quality norms for rice under PMGKAY
List-II
1. Outlay of Rs 1,27,500 crore for chip design, fabrication, equipment and talent
2. Five-year scheme with incentives of 2.25% to 5% on eligible sales
3. Support for nine new gas-based urea plants
4. Permitted broken grains in raw rice cut from 25% to 10%
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Semicon 2.0 (15 July, Rs 1,27,500 crore) builds on the first Semicon India Programme; the mobile scheme (Rs 62,500 crore) is a five-year incentive on eligible sales; NIPU 2026 backs nine gas-based urea plants, and the CCEA's rice norms (2 July) tightened broken-grain limits for foodgrains under PMGKAY. The two outlay figures are the easiest to interchange.
questions.s: Business Today and Vajiram & Ravi, 15 Jul 2026

questions.q:
The India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) entered into force on 15 July 2026, and the India-Israel Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed on 8 September 2025) came into force on 4 July 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The India-UK CETA entered into force on 15 July 2026.
2. The India-Israel Bilateral Investment Treaty came into force on 4 July 2026, nearly ten months after signing.
3. A Bilateral Investment Treaty chiefly fixes tariff rates on trade in goods between the two countries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Both entry-into-force dates are as reported. A BIT protects investors and investments (fair treatment, protection against expropriation, dispute settlement), whereas tariff schedules on goods belong to a trade agreement such as CETA. Mixing up the two instruments is a common trap.
questions.s: CTPA and Angel One, 4-17 Jul 2026

questions.q:
The Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025 (VB-G RAM G), which replaces MGNREGA, commenced nationally on 1 July 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. It replaces the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act.
2. It guarantees 100 days of work per rural household, the same as MGNREGA.
3. It sets a wage floor of Rs 300 per day.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The new law guarantees 125 days of work per rural household (MGNREGA guaranteed 100 days) and a Rs 300 per day wage floor, with a national average wage of Rs 327.4. Statement 2 therefore wrongly equates the two.
questions.s: Outlook Business, 1 Jul 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 2026, framed under the Code on Social Security, 2020, took effect on 1 July 2026.
2. The Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 2026 replaces the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 1952.
3. The CBDT's guidance note on Reporting Crypto-Asset Service Providers aligns India's crypto reporting with the IMF's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The new PF scheme is one of the instruments operationalising the labour code on social security, and it replaces the 1952 Scheme. The CBDT note (explaining Section 509 of the Income-tax Act, 2025) aligns reporting with the OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), not an IMF framework, and introduces no new tax.
questions.s: BDO India and Business Today, 1-26 Jul 2026

questions.q:
Adani Ports and SEZ agreed on 1 July 2026 to sell a 49% stake in the concessionaire of the Vizhinjam International Seaport to a subsidiary of Terminal Investment Limited, the terminal arm of MSC, for about USD 1.4 billion. Consider the following statements:
1. Kerala has objected that its prior approval is required under the 2015 concession agreement.
2. Vizhinjam, near Thiruvananthapuram, is India's first deep-water container transshipment port.
3. Kerala has said that no State approval is needed for transfer of equity in the concessionaire.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Kerala's objection rests on the concession, which treats a large equity transfer as a change in ownership requiring State approval, so statement 3 states the opposite of the State's position. Vizhinjam was built on a PPP (DBFOT) model and is meant to capture transshipment cargo that now goes through foreign hubs.
questions.s: Outlook Business and Business Today, 1 Jul 2026

questions.q:
On 23 July 2026 the United States finalised Section 301 action imposing additional duties of 10% or 12.5% on imports from 60 economies for failing to enforce bans on forced-labour imports. Consider the following statements:
1. The additional duties were finalised against 60 economies in two tiers, 10% and 12.5%.
2. India was placed in the higher 12.5% tier.
3. Section 301 of the US Trade Act of 1974 authorises the US Trade Representative to act against foreign trade practices it finds unfair or unreasonable.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India was placed in the lower 10% tier, so statement 2 is wrong. Section 301 is the USTR's investigative and retaliatory tool under the Trade Act of 1974, separate from Section 232 (national security tariffs under the Trade Expansion Act, 1962).
questions.s: KPMG TaxNewsFlash, 24 Jul 2026

questions.q:
Statement-I: India's manufacturing activity contracted in June 2026, as the HSBC India Manufacturing PMI fell to 54.2 from 55.0 in May.
Statement-II: A PMI reading above 50 signals expansion in activity over the previous month, while a reading below 50 signals contraction.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The PMI fell to 54.2 from 55.0, which is a slower pace of expansion, not a contraction, because the reading is still well above the 50 mark; Statement-I is therefore incorrect. Statement-II correctly describes the diffusion index: 50 is the no-change line.
questions.s: Tribune India, 1 Jul 2026
questions.h: 50 = the line between growth and shrink

questions.q:
On 5 August 2026 the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee announced its policy decision. Consider the following statements:
1. The repo rate was kept unchanged at 5.25%.
2. The Standing Deposit Facility rate stood at 5.00% and the Marginal Standing Facility rate at 5.50%, forming the floor and the ceiling of the liquidity adjustment corridor respectively.
3. The policy stance was changed to accommodative.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The MPC retained the repo rate at 5.25% and a neutral stance, while raising its FY27 GDP growth projection to 6.7%. The SDF (5.00%) is the floor and the MSF (5.50%) the ceiling of the corridor around the repo rate, so statement 2 is correct; statement 3 is wrong because the stance remained neutral.
questions.s: Free Press Journal and SCC Online, 5 Aug 2026

questions.q:
Alongside its August 2026 policy, the RBI released draft guidelines to resume on-tap licensing of Urban Co-operative Banks (UCBs), which has been paused since 2004. Consider the following statements:
1. The licensing of new UCBs had been paused since 2004 and the draft guidelines propose to resume on-tap licensing.
2. The draft proposes a minimum net worth of Rs 300 crore and a net NPA not above 3% for eligibility.
3. UCBs are regulated solely by the Ministry of Cooperation, and the RBI has no regulatory role over them.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 follow the draft released on 5 August 2026 (other draft criteria include at least ten years of operation and CRAR of 12%). UCBs come under dual regulation: the RBI regulates their banking business (licensing, capital, NPAs), while the cooperative registrar regulates management aspects, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Drishti IAS and Vision IAS, 5 Aug 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers Disclosure Scheme (FAST-DS), 2026 came into force on 16 August 2026 and declarations can be filed only until 31 December 2026.
2. The Lok Sabha passed the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 on 6 August 2026, replacing the Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026.
3. The Central Board of Direct Taxes functions under the Department of Expenditure of the Ministry of Finance.
4. The Bill extended the tax exemption for foreign firms supplying capital goods to Indian electronics contract manufacturers to the tax year ending 31 March 2031.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The CBDT is a part of the Department of Revenue, not Expenditure, and the electronics exemption was extended to the tax year ending 31 March 2041, not 2031. A Bill that replaces an Ordinance must be passed within six weeks of Parliament reassembling or the Ordinance lapses (Article 123).
questions.s: All India Radio and Business Today, 6-16 Aug 2026

questions.q: From 3 August 2026, SEBI's Closing Auction Session for stocks in the F&O segment discovers a single equilibrium closing price through an auction held between 3:30 and 3:35 pm. The closing price of these stocks was earlier arrived at by
o: the last traded price of the day
a simple average of the day's high and low prices
the opening price of the next trading day
a volume-weighted average price (VWAP) based closing price
questions.e: The auction replaces the VWAP-based closing price with one equilibrium price from matched buy and sell orders, which is harder to manipulate through last-minute trades. Continuous trading for F&O stocks ends at 3:15 pm, and other stocks continue to trade till 3:30 pm.
questions.s: Outlook Business and Bigul, 3 Aug 2026

questions.q:
The Unified Payments Interface completed ten years on 25 August 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. UPI completed ten years on 25 August 2026.
2. UPI is operated directly by the Reserve Bank of India as a department of the central bank.
3. Annual UPI transactions rose from about 1.78 crore in FY 2016-17 to more than 24,000 crore in FY 2025-26.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: UPI is run by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), an umbrella organisation for retail payments promoted by the RBI and banks, not by the RBI itself. The growth from about 1.78 crore to over 24,000 crore annual transactions in a decade shows how UPI became the main retail payments rail.
questions.s: Outlook Business/PTI, 25 Aug 2026

questions.q:
The Department of Consumer Affairs notified the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 in August 2026, making Indian Standard Time the common legal time reference. Consider the following statements:
1. The Rules are made under Section 52 of the Legal Metrology Act, 2009 and take effect 180 days after publication in the Gazette.
2. Indian Standard Time is based on the 82.5 degrees East meridian and is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of UTC.
3. ISRO is the custodian of Indian Standard Time.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: IST is defined on the 82.5 degrees East meridian (UTC+5:30). The custodian of IST is the CSIR-National Physical Laboratory, not ISRO, although the Rules promote the use of NavIC for time distribution.
questions.s: All India Radio and Drishti IAS, 27 Aug 2026

questions.q:
India's foreign exchange reserves reached an all-time high of USD 729.33 billion as of 21 August 2026, driven by the RBI's concessional swap window for FCNR(B) deposits. Consider the following statements:
1. The reserves touched a record USD 729.33 billion as of 21 August 2026.
2. The record reserves were driven by the RBI's concessional swap window for FCNR(B) deposits.
3. FCNR(B) deposits are Indian rupee deposits that non-resident Indians can hold only in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: FCNR(B) stands for Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) deposits, which are held in designated foreign currencies, not in rupees; the RBI's swap window lets banks swap these dollar inflows at a concessional rate. A similar window was used in 2013 under Governor Raghuram Rajan to shore up reserves and the rupee.
questions.s: Drishti IAS, 29 Aug 2026

questions.q:
On 24 September 2026 the Centre cut the Basic Customs Duty on crude edible oils ahead of the festival season. Consider the following statements:
1. The duty on crude sunflower oil was reduced from 10% to nil.
2. The duty on crude soybean oil and crude palm oil was reduced to 5%.
3. The cut raises the landed cost of imported crude edible oils and so protects domestic oilseed farmers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A customs duty cut lowers the landed price of imported oil, which helps moderate retail prices; it does not raise it, so statement 3 is reversed. Keeping a duty differential between crude and refined oil continues to support domestic refining.
questions.s: Telangana Today and AIR News, 24 Sep 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. On 2 September 2026 Japan Credit Rating Agency upgraded India's long-term sovereign ratings from BBB+ to A- with a Stable outlook.
2. On 16 September 2026 the US Federal Reserve's FOMC raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00%, its first rate hike since 2023.
3. RBI's preliminary balance of payments data for April-June 2026 showed the current account deficit widening to US$4.2 billion, or 0.5% of GDP.
4. The balance of payments data is compiled and released quarterly by the National Statistics Office, MoSPI.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Balance of payments data are compiled and released quarterly by the RBI, so statement 4 is wrong; the other three are as reported. A Fed hike tends to pull capital towards the US, pressuring the rupee and emerging-market flows, which is why it matters for RBI policy.
questions.s: AIR News, Central Banking and ThePrint, Sep 2026

questions.q:
Statement-I: A framework approved in September 2026 applies a 0.4% Merchant Discount Rate on UPI merchant payments above Rs 2,000 from 15 October 2026, while person-to-person UPI transfers remain free.
Statement-II: The Merchant Discount Rate is the fee that a merchant pays to the banks and payment intermediaries for accepting a digital payment.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct, but Statement-II only defines MDR; it does not explain why the framework charges 0.4% above Rs 2,000 (the aim is to fund the payments ecosystem while shielding small merchants and person-to-person transfers). Zero-MDR on UPI had been in place since 2020.
questions.s: Moneylife, 16 Sep 2026

questions.q:
Sagarmala Finance Corporation scheduled India's first blue bond for 28 September 2026, a Rs 600 crore base issue with a Rs 500 crore greenshoe option. Consider the following statements:
1. It is India's first blue bond, raised by a state-owned maritime lender.
2. A greenshoe option allows the issuer to retain a part of the subscription received in excess of the base issue size.
3. Blue bonds are meant mainly to finance projects on forests and terrestrial biodiversity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Blue bonds finance ocean and water-related sustainable projects (here maritime lending, greenfield ports and coastal roads), not forests or terrestrial biodiversity, so statement 3 is wrong. The greenshoe lets the issuer keep oversubscription up to the stated extra amount (here Rs 500 crore).
questions.s: GKToday and Maritime Gateway, 28 Sep 2026

questions.q:
In September 2026 the Prime Minister dedicated the last sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, completing the full route from JNPT (Maharashtra) to Dadri (Uttar Pradesh). Consider the following statements:
1. The Western DFC now runs the full route from JNPT in Maharashtra to Dadri in Uttar Pradesh.
2. The Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors are built by the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited, a public sector company under the Ministry of Railways.
3. The Western DFC terminates at Sonnagar in Bihar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Western DFC links JNPT with Dadri; Sonnagar is the eastern terminus of the Eastern DFC, which comes from Ludhiana, so statement 3 mixes the two corridors. DFCCIL builds both corridors for the Ministry of Railways.
questions.s: Maritime Gateway and Free Press Journal, 8 Sep 2026

questions.q:
On 18 September 2026 the National Statistics Office released its first district-level Periodic Labour Force Survey estimates, titled 'Labour Market Snapshot of Selected Districts'. Consider the following statements:
1. The release used the revised sampling design introduced in January 2025.
2. The PLFS is conducted by the National Statistics Office under MoSPI.
3. The PLFS is conducted by the Labour Bureau of the Ministry of Labour and Employment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The PLFS is an NSO (MoSPI) survey that measures indicators such as the labour force participation rate, worker population ratio and unemployment rate; it is not a Labour Bureau survey. Earlier PLFS releases were available only at State level, so district-level estimates are a first.
questions.s: The Policy Edge and Anantam IAS, 18 Sep 2026

questions.q:
The United Kingdom recognised India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme as a qualifying carbon-pricing mechanism for relief under the UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (September 2026). Consider the following statements:
1. The recognition prevents Indian exporters from paying dual carbon charges.
2. India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme is a domestic compliance carbon market.
3. The recognition fully exempts all Indian exports from the UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A carbon border mechanism taxes the embedded carbon in imports, but gives credit for a carbon price already paid at home; recognition of the CCTS therefore removes double charging and does not exempt exports. Statement 3 over-generalises.
questions.s: AIR News and Outlook Business, 8 Sep 2026

questions.q:
On 25 September 2026 the Finance Ministry announced the Centre's market borrowing plan for the second half of FY2026-27. Consider the following statements:
1. The Centre will borrow Rs 7.86 lakh crore through dated securities in October-March 2026-27.
2. The annual market borrowing has been cut by about Rs 1.2 lakh crore from the Budget estimate.
3. The RBI, as the government's debt manager, manages the borrowing calendar and auctions.
4. Dated securities are short-term instruments that mature in less than 91 days.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Dated securities are long-term government bonds (usually with maturities of five to forty years), whereas treasury bills of 91, 182 and 364 days are the short-term instruments. The first three statements are as announced or follow from the RBI's role as debt manager of the Centre and States.
questions.s: ThePrint and Deccan Chronicle, 25 Sep 2026

questions.q:
On 15 September 2026 the Central Consumer Protection Authority imposed a Rs 10 lakh penalty on Rapido's operator for misleading advance-payment and tipping prompts amounting to dark patterns. Consider the following statements:
1. The CCPA imposed a penalty of Rs 10 lakh and directed discontinuation of the prompts.
2. The CCPA is the regulator set up under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
3. Under the amended E-Commerce Rules effective 1 January 2027, the 'prior price' for a discount is the highest price charged in the preceding 30 days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Under the amended rules, notified on 10 September 2026 and effective 1 January 2027, the 'prior price' is the lowest offer price in the preceding 30 days. Using the highest price would make 'discounts' easy to inflate, which is exactly the misleading-discount practice the rules target.
questions.s: Business Today and ThePrint, 15 Sep 2026
